column1: # Polyphonic substitution cipher used by Duke of Mayenne, commander de Diou (ambassador in Rome for the
# Catholic League) and others, 1592-93. Reconstructed by S. Tomokiyo from letters in BnF fr.3982 (f.97,
# f.101, f.124), fr.3983 (f.106, f.108v, f.211); fr.4715 f.61 flagged as the same cipher, undeciphered.
# Source image: sources/cryptiana/web/mayenne.png (from mayenne.htm, fetched 24 Sept 2026).
# NOT the cipher used in fr.2751 (that item's own encipherment is unread this pass, see NOTES.md) --
# captured here only for a later mechanical trial against a transcribed fr.2751 ciphertext.
# Layout: the source table stacks two alphabet rows (a-m over n-z) at the same column positions and
# draws mostly ONE glyph per column -- i.e. the column for "a" is directly above the column for "n" and
# most columns show a single symbol, consistent with Tomokiyo's text noting confusable "similar" symbols
# for the pairs a/n, c/p, d/q (some columns, a/n and d/q here, show two stacked glyph variants instead of
# one). sign = this repo's code; value = both letters the column stands for, pipe-separated where the
# image shows two stacked glyphs, else the pair as given by the layout. Grade M throughout: small
# (~55x90px) web thumbnail, glyph identity within the crowded "hash/cross" family (columns b/o, c/p, d/q,
# e/r, h/u) is not reliably distinguishable at this resolution. Re-derive from the BnF fr.3982/3983 page
# images directly before use in a real trial.
